results.title: SWE-bench Evaluation Harness: Fixing Docker Errors
results.content:
The SWE-bench evaluation harness builds a tall stack of Docker images and runs each task in its own container. That design is what makes the scores reproducible, and it is also where the setup pain lives. Disk fills up, an image fails to build, a run stalls, or a Mac tries to pull an image that does not exist for its chip. [...] Docker's virtual disk is too small for the image stack. The harness needs roughly 120 GB of free disk, so raise Docker Desktop's disk image size and prune old images. This is the cause behind issue #144, where a run dies while building environment images.

 

### How much disk space does SWE-bench need? [...] SWE-bench builds images in three layers: a base image, then environment images, then per-task instance images. The environment layer alone spans dozens of images, and the full prebuilt set runs into hundreds of gigabytes uncached. Seeing the layering is what makes the cache setting make sense.
